instances.summary: While the game calculates my move's power, a single-hit damaging slicing or pulse move gets its power multiplied by 0.7. Crosscut uses 0.7 so each of its two strikes is weaker.
While I have this, in doubles I take 50% of the direct damage aimed at my ally. In singles, after I switch out on purpose, my replacement sends 25% of direct damage to me for 1 turn(s).
When I enter, my base Speed and the fastest foe's base Speed are swapped. At the end of each of the next 3 turns, a share of the original gap returns, until both are back to normal.
At the end of every turn, a Speed swap I started when I entered returns one more step, until both Pokemon have their own base Speed back. It does nothing if no swap is running.
Each time I knock out a Pokemon, my ally with the lowest HP heals 10% of its max HP. From knockout number 2 of the turn on, the ally is also cured of its status.
Once per battle, when an attack would knock out my ally, it stays at 1 HP and the attacker is Drenched for 2 turns (it moves last in its priority bracket).
When I enter I link to my nearest living ally. When that ally faints I gain 1 stages in Speed and my higher attacking stat and lose 1 stages in Defense and Sp. Def. No ally, no effect.
Records the first move each foe uses (the last 3 are kept). A recorded move used again on a later turn does x0.85 damage to my side. I can cast recorded moves, 2 PP per battle shared.
Before I use a move, I change into the form linked to that move's type; a Normal-type move returns me to my base form. A form without its own moves gets 3 from its learnset.
When I enter, the foe across from me gains the Dragon type on top of its own. Later, a foe I damage with a biting move or a Dragon-type move gains it too.
While I have this, when I hit one foe with a single-target biting move or a Dragon-type move, up to 2 side heads also hit other Dragon-type foes with it at 35% power and no side effects.
When I enter, every foe gains the types of 1 other living teammate(s) of its own team, as extra types. Foes that come in later are changed too, and it is undone when I leave.
Each time I use a Psychic-type move, damaging or not, the terrain changes to Psychic. A terrain that is already up is left alone.
